values.note: recreation.gov: $23 a standard site in 2026 and 2027 ($52 a double site, $29 an equestrian site). The Forest Service page says 'Single Site: $28 per night'. One RV per single site; an extra vehicle pays a nightly fee collected at the campground.

fees.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/253680/rates (Peak Season 2026-05-13 to 2026-11-01 and 2027-05-13 to 2027-10-31: STANDARD NONELECTRIC 23, EQUESTRIAN NONELECTRIC 29, double STANDARD NONELECTRIC 52) + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/whiteriver/recreation/marvine-campground ('Single Site: $28 per night', last updated June 8, 2026), read 2026-10-26

hookups.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/253680 ('Electrical hook-ups are not available') + per-site catalog (all 22 sites STANDARD/EQUESTRIAN NONELECTRIC, no water or sewer hookup), read 2026-10-26

values.note: 17 standard sites in loops 1-2 (max vehicle 20-40 ft; 6 pull-throughs, three of them 40 ft) and 5 equestrian sites with corrals in their own loop 3, for campers with stock only (the FS page says six). Several standard spurs take only 20 ft.

sites.source: recreation.gov per-site catalog for 253680 (loops 1-2: 17 STANDARD NONELECTRIC, Max Vehicle Length 20-40, Pull-Through sites 2, 4, 5, 11, 14, 18; loop 3: 5 EQUESTRIAN NONELECTRIC, equipment Horse) + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/whiteriver/recreation/marvine-campground ('Marvine has six horse campsites with corrals for campers with stock only. Campers inside the main campground may not use these corrals'), read 2026-10-26

values.note: No water in 2026: the Forest Service says the well is dry, so bring all you need (recreation.gov still describes hand-pump drinking water). Bear-proof food lockers at each site; trash service.

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/whiteriver/recreation/marvine-campground ('There is no water at the campground due to the well being dry'; 'Potable water is not available at this site'; 'Vault Toilet'; alert 'Water not available at Lowry, Prospector, Windy Point and Marvine Campgrounds') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/253680 ('vault toilets and hand pump drinking water. Trash service is provided'; 'Bear-proof food lockers are provided at each site'), read 2026-10-26

values.note: Every site is reservable on recreation.gov; 2026 season May 13 - Nov 1 (2027: May 13 - Oct 31), closing 2 days before arrival. No minimum stay (weekend minimums set to 0). 14 nights at most, and 14 a month. A site must be occupied the first night; reserved sites are held until 11 am the next day. Run for the Forest Service by American Land & Leisure.

booking.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/253680 (facility_rules maxConsecutiveStay 14, maxStay 14 'Each Month', minWeekendStay 0 soft, minHolidayWeekendStay 0 soft, reservationCutOff 2; notices quoted; 'Help.WhiteRiver.Blanco@AmericanLL.com') + /rates (Peak Season dates) + per-site catalog (22 of 22 reservable), read 2026-10-26

note: Blanco RD, White River NF: 8,200 ft in conifer and aspen on Marvine Creek, 35 mi east of Meeker (the last 6 mi on Rio Blanco CR 12). Marvine and East Marvine trails into the Flat Tops Wilderness start beside it, toward Marvine Lakes. The horse sites sit in their own loop. --Claude
summary: This is the family campground: loops 1-2 hold the 17 standard sites, and the stock sites are a separate equestrian loop 3 'for campers with stock only' (East Marvine next door is the other, non-reservable camp), so no horse-camp issue. Recorded rec.gov's $23 (2026, 2027; FS says $28), no hookups, 22 sites to 40 ft with pull-throughs, reservable season May 13 - Nov 1, 2-day cutoff, 14-night limit, no minimum. Facilities: vault toilets; potable water false for now (well dry, FS 2026). Operating season not stated anywhere (left). Pin 120 m from the catalog centroid. No road closure alert for CR 8/12.
flags: Fee conflict: recreation.gov's 2026 and 2027 rate tables charge $23 for a standard site; the Forest Service page (updated June 8, 2026) says 'Single Site: $28 per night'. Recorded $23.

Water: the FS page and an active alert say there is no water ('the well being dry'); recreation.gov still advertises 'hand pump drinking water'. Recorded potable_water false with the reason in the note.
